Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for negative slice bounds, so any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. The accompanying comments (\"underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically\", \"safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level\") are factually wrong; there is no permission check in this code path. Previously negative offsets were effectively bounded; this change removes that safety. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`."},
  {"file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py", "line": 70, "severity": "high", "category": "security", "title": "Unvetted `optimized_pagination` query flag switches audit logs to an unsafe paginator", "body": "A client-controlled query parameter (`optimized_pagination=true`) selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, enabling the negative-offset code path. Additionally `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime')))` on a datetime field, which raises TypeError — so the optimized branch is broken for the `-datetime` ordering used here and will 500. Also, later code still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`, so when clamping occurs the extra-row trim check no longer matches and an extra row can leak into the page. Either clamp uniformly and use the clamped value in the comparison, or raise on negative offsets."},

The previous behavior (dropping the whole oversized segment with `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` + error log) was observable; now data loss is invisible. If a union ran, the count can be lower than the actual cardinality, so a segment can exceed the cap, or (if a union inflated the count) spans can be evicted unnecessarily. findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative offsets, exposing data outside pagination bounds / 500s
findings.body: The `enable_advanced_features` branch passes `cursor.offset` (negative) directly into a Django queryset slice: `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for negative slice bounds, so any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. The accompanying comments ("underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") are factually wrong; there is no permission check in this code path. Previously negative offsets were effectively bounded; this change removes that safety. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: Unvetted `optimized_pagination` query flag switches audit logs to an unsafe paginator
findings.body: A client-controlled query parameter (`optimized_pagination=true`) selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, enabling the negative-offset code path. Any org member with `has_global_access` (not just admins, contrary to the comment) can trigger it. Additionally `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime')))` on a datetime field, which raises TypeError — so the optimized branch is broken for the `-datetime` ordering used here and will 500. This feature flag should not be user-selectable and the paginator must handle datetime keys.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError on `organization_context.member`
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` (e.g. for superusers or non-member access via RpcUserOrganizationContext), so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise AttributeError and 500 the endpoint. Short-circuiting is unreliable because `request.user.is_superuser` may be False for non-member staff/token access.

findings.title: BasePaginator offset clamping changes prev-page semantics inconsistently
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only for next-page cursors, while `is_prev` cursors still pass a possibly negative offset into the queryset slice (AssertionError in Django). Also, later code still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`, so when clamping occurs the extra-row trim check no longer matches and an extra row can leak into the page. Either clamp uniformly and use the clamped value in the comparison, or raise on negative offsets.

findings.title: Hardcoded 1000-span cap silently drops spans and ignores max_segment_spans config
findings.body: Eviction uses a literal `1000` instead of the configurable `max_segment_spans` (1001 in SpansBuffer), and `zpopmin` silently discards the oldest spans with no metric or log. The previous behavior (dropping the whole oversized segment with `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` + error log) was observable; now data loss is invisible. Pass the limit in as an ARGV and emit a metric/return the number evicted.

findings.title: span_count may be stale, causing over- or under-eviction
findings.body: `span_count` is set from the result of `zunionstore` calls, but when both unions run the second overwrites the first, and in either case the count reflects the set state before the Python-side `zadd` of new payloads in this batch happens relative to other pipeline commands. Only when `span_count == 0` is `zcard` consulted. If a union ran, the count can be lower than the actual cardinality, so a segment can exceed the cap, or (if a union inflated the count) spans can be evicted unnecessarily. Always read `zcard set_key` right before the cap check.

findings.title: Redirect-chain loop limit reduced 10000 -> 1000 without justification, and explanatory comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the comment warning that chains deeper than the bound may not be joined correctly was deleted. Segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will now silently fail to merge, producing split segments. This is unrelated to the eviction change; if intentional it needs a metric/alert and a comment, otherwise restore 10000.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead config while enforcement moved to a Lua literal
findings.body: `self.max_segment_spans` is still a constructor parameter but no longer used anywhere after the span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the limit is hardcoded as 1000 in add-buffer.lua. Operators tuning `max_segment_spans` will have no effect, and the two values (1001 vs 1000) disagree. Wire the parameter through to the script or remove it.

findings.title: zadd keyed on payload: duplicate payloads collapse and score is overwritten
findings.body: Switching from `sadd` to `zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})` makes the payload the sorted-set member. Two spans with byte-identical payloads still collapse to one entry (same as the set), but now re-ingesting a span also rewrites its score, which changes its eviction priority. More importantly, eviction by `zpopmin` on `end_timestamp_precise` drops the *earliest-ending* spans — typically the root/parent spans of a segment — rather than the least useful ones, which can destroy segment structure. Worth documenting/justifying, and the module docstring (lines 39-44, 58) still describes these keys as "sets" with `sadd` semantics.

findings.title: __reduce__ omits new/existing fields, so pickled buffers lose configuration
findings.body: `__reduce__` only passes `assigned_shards`, the two timeouts and `redis_ttl`, dropping `segment_page_size`, `max_segment_bytes` and `max_segment_spans`. In multiprocessing mode the buffer is pickled to subprocesses, so any non-default values for those limits are silently reset to defaults in workers.

findings.title: No test for the new eviction-during-insert behavior
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is eviction during insert, but tests only add the now-required `end_timestamp_precise` field. There is no test that inserts more than the cap into one segment and asserts which spans are retained/evicted, nor a test that the removed `max_segment_spans` read-path behavior is covered by the new Lua cap. Regressions in the eviction arithmetic (stale `span_count`, off-by-one in `span_count - 1000`) would go undetected.

findings.title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator has no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a new public paginator wired into a production endpoint but has no unit tests covering next/prev cursors, negative offsets, or the datetime key path. Given it duplicates ~60 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result` with subtle differences, untested divergence is likely.
